parts.subtitle: What Manifest is, how to sign in and get around, who does what, and the one shared pool of money.

chapters.title: Welcome to Manifest
chapters.html:
Manifest is the shared workspace where Legend of Toys (LOT) and Solve Factory (SF) run every China import together. It replaces the old WhatsApp-and-spreadsheet way of tracking orders and money with one live system both sides can see.

What it’s for
Tracking China orders end to end, with one shared money pool.
Who uses it
LOT Solve Factory
Two sides
LOT requests & funds. SF runs the lifecycle.
Live
Always current; dates stamp automatically.

The idea in one paragraph

LOT asks for what it needs and puts money into a shared pool. SF takes it from there: it raises the purchase order with the Chinese vendor, pays the vendor, ships the goods, clears customs, delivers to LOT’s warehouse, and finally invoices LOT to close the order. Everything is tracked live, with a full timestamped history on every order and every shipment, so anyone can look back and see exactly what happened and when.

The golden rule of who does what

LOT

Raises the request and funds the shared pool. That is essentially it.

Solve Factory

Owns the entire lifecycle after the request: converting it to a real PO, paying the vendor, shipping, customs, delivery, and invoicing LOT.

What this manual covers

This is a combined system and process guide. Each chapter explains what the step is in the real import process, and then exactly how to do it on the screen. Read the Getting Started part first; after that, the parts follow the natural order of a shipment, from request to invoice.

ⓘ Note

Manifest is the first LOT system with external users. Solve Factory signs in with an email link (no Google account needed), and the system only ever shows SF what it should see.

chapters.title: Signing In & Getting Around
chapters.html:
Manifest opens as a single live dashboard with a sidebar. How you sign in depends on which side you are: LOT signs in with Google, Solve Factory signs in with an email link.

LOT sign-in
Sign in with Google (legendoftoys.com).
SF sign-in
Partner sign-in by email link.
Layout
Left sidebar, top bar, one main screen.
Address
manifest.legendoftoys.com

Signing in

LOT team

Use Sign in with Google with your legendoftoys.com account. This is the same login you use for the other LOT systems.

Solve Factory

  1. Request a link. On the sign-in screen, choose Partner sign-in and enter your email.
  2. Open the email. Click the secure link Manifest sends you. No password, no Google account needed.
  3. First time only. An LOT admin onboards you once so the system knows who you are. After that, the email link is all you need.
⚠ Watch out

If a login link opens Manifest but it says you have no access, you have not been onboarded yet. Ask an LOT admin to add you (Admin chapter).

Getting around

Sidebar

Jump between Dashboard, Orders, Shipments, the money screens (Running Account, Draw-downs, Payments, Exchange Rates), Documents and Admin. SF sees a trimmed set.

Top bar

Shows where you are, the live CNY to INR rate, and a green LIVE dot when data is current.

Detail screens

Click any order or shipment row to open its detail, where all the actions live. A back chip returns you to the list.

Tweaks

The small dial at the bottom-right sets the accent colour and density. It only changes how the app looks for you.

✓ Tip

The app is always live. After you record something, the numbers refresh on their own; you rarely need to reload the page.

chapters.title: Who Does What
chapters.html:
Manifest has two parties, LOT and Solve Factory, plus an Admin layer. What you can see and do depends on which party you are and which role you hold.

Parties
LOT and Solve Factory (SF).
LOT does
Requests, funds the pool, views all.
SF does
Runs the whole lifecycle.
Cost lens
SF never sees LOT’s internal cost columns.

The roles

RolePartyCan do
LOT Finance / FounderLOTCreate requests, record LOT to SF wires, see every order, shipment and the running account.
Solve Factory OwnerSFConvert requests to POs, place them, attach the PI, pay the vendor and logistics, run shipments, invoice and close orders.
AdminLOTEverything, plus manage users and roles, the shipment timeline defaults, and the logistics-partner master.

What each side sees

LOT

The full picture: every order, every shipment, all payments and the running account. LOT funds the pool and watches it.

Solve Factory

A trimmed sidebar focused on running orders and shipments and recording what it pays. SF never sees LOT’s internal cost-per-unit or margin columns, by design.

ⓘ Note

Most of the work after a request belongs to SF. If you are on the LOT side, your main jobs are raising the request and keeping the pool funded.

⛔ Important

Admin can act on SF’s behalf (for example to drive or correct an order) because LOT runs the system. Use that carefully: the audit trail records who did what.

chapters.title: The Shared Pool, in Plain English
chapters.html:
There is one shared pool of money between LOT and Solve Factory. Think of it as a running tab. Understanding the pool is the key to understanding every money screen in Manifest.

LOT pays in
Pool goes up. SF holds LOT’s money.
SF spends out
Pool goes down, the moment it’s paid.
Balance
Can be positive or negative.
Truth
Always live to what has actually been paid.

How the pool moves

Pool positive

Solve Factory is holding LOT’s money, ready to spend on the next order.

Pool negative

SF has spent more than LOT has put in, so LOT owes SF. This is allowed and normal; SF recovers it as LOT funds the pool again.

The most important money rule

⛔ Important

Every payment SF makes is deducted from the pool the moment it is recorded, not later at invoice time. So the pool is always accurate to whatever has actually been paid out on LOT’s behalf.

Everything SF pays, and when

PaymentWhenAgainst
Vendor advanceAfter the vendor PI is receivedthe order
Pickup balance / extra servicesAt pickupthe order
ShippingWhen the goods clear the portthe shipment
Customs / dutyWhen the goods clear the portthe shipment
Other port feesWhen the goods clear the portthe shipment
Last-mile deliveryPort to warehousethe shipment
SF commission (2.5%)At invoicethe order

The first two wrap up the goods purchase. The middle four are logistics. The last is SF’s fee. Every one of them reduces the pool the moment it is recorded.

ⓘ Note

Invoicing is a close-out record, not a money move. The money for goods and logistics already left the pool as it was paid. See the Invoicing chapter.

parts.subtitle: One continuous flow: LOT requests, SF builds the PO and drives it all the way to an invoice.

chapters.title: How an Order Flows
chapters.html:
An order in Manifest flows through one continuous, party-owned lifecycle. LOT starts it with a request; Solve Factory drives it the rest of the way to a closed invoice. This chapter is the map; the next chapters are the steps.

Starts with
LOT raises a request.
Driven by
SF, all the way to invoice.
Ends with
Invoiced (closed).
History
Every move is timestamped.

The journey, end to end

  1. LOT requests it. The order is Requested. This is the only thing LOT does to the order itself.
  2. SF converts it to a PO. SF fills the vendor, the vendor’s product codes and the prices in Yuan. The order becomes Draft.
  3. SF places the PO. The order becomes Placed and a printable PO document unlocks. SF sends it to the vendor.
  4. Vendor sends the PI; SF attaches it. Stored as evidence and stamped on the timeline.
  5. SF pays the advance. Deducts the pool.
  6. Production to pickup. Confirmed, Produced, Picked up. At pickup SF pays any balance. Goods purchase is now wrapped up.
  7. SF ships it. Onto a shipment (air or sea), then sailing, docking, customs, last-mile. Costs paid along the way.
  8. Delivered. The goods reach the warehouse.
  9. SF invoices LOT. Partially invoiced, then Invoiced once everything is billed.

The states an order moves through

Lifecycle

Requested → Draft → Placed → Confirmed → Produced → Picked up → Shipped → Received → Delivered, plus Cancelled.

Billing

Runs in parallel near the end: In flight → Delivered → Partially invoiced → Invoiced.

The short version (cheat sheet)

  1. LOT requests, LOT funds the pool. Everything else is SF.
  2. One shared pool. Every SF payment deducts it the moment it’s recorded.
  3. SF flow. Convert, place (PO PDF), attach PI, pay advance, produce, pickup (pay balance), ship, clear customs (pay shipping/customs/fees), deliver (pay last-mile), invoice.
  4. Cancellable until pickup, never after.
  5. Invoice is a close-out record. Partial allowed; GST editable per line; optional 2.5% commission.
⛔ Important

An order can be cancelled at any time up to and including Produced. Once it is Picked up, it can no longer be cancelled, because the goods are paid for and on their way.

chapters.title: Step 1 - LOT Requests an Order
chapters.html:
A request is how LOT tells Solve Factory what it needs from China. It is the only thing LOT does to the order itself; SF takes over from there.

Who
LOT Admin
Where
Orders → New Order
Creates
An order in Requested state.
Next
SF converts it to a PO.

Raising a request

  1. Open New Order. On the Orders screen, click New Order.
  2. Choose “Request”. In the Create card, set Create as to request.
  3. Give it a title. Plain and recognisable, for example Ghost 500 or Nitro restock.
  4. Pick a category. Product, Part, Sub-part, Mould, Sample or Other.
  5. Add the items you want (optional). Product, quantity and, if you know it, a per-unit price. SF will firm these up.
  6. Create request. The order appears in the list as Requested.

What happens next

The request sits in Requested until Solve Factory picks it up and converts it to a PO. From that point SF owns it: vendor, pricing, shipping, payments and invoicing. You can keep watching it on the Orders list and its detail page.

ⓘ Note

A request is deliberately light. You do not need vendor names, Yuan prices or shipping details; that is SF’s job at conversion. Just describe what you need clearly.

✓ Tip

Putting the quantity in the title (for example Ghost 500) makes the Orders list easy to scan at a glance.

chapters.title: Step 2 - SF Converts to a PO & Places It
chapters.html:
Converting a request to a PO is where Solve Factory takes ownership. SF fills in the real purchase-order detail in the vendor’s own product codes, then places it and sends the PO document to the vendor.

Who
Solve Factory Admin
Where
Order detail (open a Requested order)
Moves
Requested → Draft → Placed
Unlocks
A printable PO document at Placed.

Convert, then fill the PO

  1. Open the request. Click it in the Orders list. While it is Requested, you see a Convert to PO button.
  2. Convert to PO. The order moves to Draft and becomes fully editable by SF.
  3. Edit the lines. For each item set the vendor item code, a description, the quantity and the unit price in Yuan. A single PO can mix items on different GST codes; set GST per line later at invoice.
  4. Add costs. Use Edit on the order to record purchase, shipping and customs as they become known. Goods are priced in Yuan; landed cost builds up as it ships.

Why the PO uses the vendor’s codes

The PO is written in the Chinese vendor’s product codes, not LOT’s names. For example, the product LOT calls Flare may appear on the vendor’s PO as 820D. Manifest stores both: the vendor item code and a readable product name.

ⓘ Note

Because the PO speaks vendor codes, Manifest does not push it into Snorkel (LOT’s procurement system) automatically. Bridging the two needs a separate vendor-code to LOT-product connector, which is planned but not built yet. Until then Manifest runs fully on its own.

Place the PO

  1. Place order. When the PO is ready, click Place order. The order moves to Placed and the timeline starts.
  2. Download the PO PDF. A printable, vendor-facing PO (in Yuan, in vendor codes) becomes available. Send it to the vendor.
⚠ Watch out

The PO PDF is a clean placeholder format for now. SF’s preferred layout will be folded in later; the numbers and codes are correct, the styling will improve.

chapters.title: Step 3 - Vendor PI & the Advance
chapters.html:
Once the PO is placed and sent, the vendor replies with a Proforma Invoice (PI). SF attaches it as evidence and then pays the vendor advance out of the shared pool.

Who
Solve Factory Admin
PI
Uploaded as evidence, stamped on the timeline.
Advance
Paid from the pool, after the PI.
Pool
Drops the moment the advance is recorded.

Attaching the vendor PI

  1. Open the order. Go to the order’s detail page.
  2. Upload the PI. Add the vendor’s Proforma Invoice as a document of type PI.
  3. It becomes a milestone. Manifest stamps a timestamped PI attached event on the order timeline, so everyone can see when it landed.
ⓘ Note

Manifest never generates the PI. It only stores the vendor’s, as evidence.

Paying the advance

  1. Open Vendor payment. On the order detail, click Record in the Vendor payment card.
  2. Choose the type. Set it to advance.
  3. Enter the amount. The amount in Yuan and the actual bank rate you paid at. Manifest shows the rupee value it will deduct.
  4. Record payment. The pool drops immediately by that amount.
⛔ Important

Always enter the actual bank rate you paid at, not the reference rate. The vendor advance is real money leaving the pool on LOT’s behalf.

✓ Tip

If recording the advance pushes the pool negative, Manifest nudges you to raise a draw-down so LOT can top the pool up. It is a prompt, not a block: SF can still pay from its own pocket.

chapters.title: Step 4 - Production, Pickup & Cancelling
chapters.html:
After the advance, SF moves the order through production and pays the balance at pickup. This is also the last point at which an order can be cancelled.

Who
Solve Factory Admin
Stages
Confirmed → Produced → Picked up
At pickup
Pay the balance / extra services.
Cancel cut-off
Up to Produced, never after pickup.

Advancing production

  1. Advance the stage. On the order detail, use the Advance button to move Confirmed → Produced → Picked up as the vendor progresses. Each step is date-stamped automatically.
  2. Pay the pickup balance. At pickup, record any remaining balance or extra services as a vendor payment with type pickup balance. It deducts the pool right away.

At this point the goods purchase is fully wrapped up: advance plus pickup balance. What follows is logistics.

Cancelling an order

⛔ Important

An order can be cancelled at any time up to and including Produced. Once it is Picked up, it can no longer be cancelled, because the goods are paid for and on their way.

  1. Open the order. While it is Requested, Draft, Placed, Confirmed or Produced, a Cancel button is shown.
  2. Give a reason. A reason is required and is logged on the timeline.
  3. Confirm. The order moves to Cancelled.
⚠ Watch out

Cancelling does not automatically reverse any payments already made on the order. Those stay as pool debits and are reconciled by hand. This is deliberate; the system stays honest about money that actually moved.

parts.subtitle: Getting the goods from the Chinese vendor to the LOT warehouse, by air or by sea.

chapters.title: How Shipments Work (Air vs Sea)
chapters.html:
A shipment is one physical container with its own schedule. Once goods are picked up, SF puts them on a shipment and tracks it from the factory to the LOT warehouse. Every shipment is either Air or Sea.

Who
Solve Factory Admin
Two modes
Air and Sea, same steps.
Lock point
Contents lock once it departs.
Mixing
One container can carry several POs.

The shipment journey

Sea

Planned → Loaded → Sailing → Docked → Cleared → Local transport → Received.

Air

The same steps, read as Planned → Loaded → In Flight → Landed → Cleared → Local transport → Received.

Each milestone is date-stamped automatically as SF advances it.

Air vs Sea, what’s different

AspectSeaAir
Speed (door to door)roughly 30 to 40 daysroughly 5 to 8 days
Freight basisper container or volumechargeable weight
Carrier documentBill of Lading (BL)Air Waybill (AWB)
WordingSailing / DockedIn Flight / Landed

The steps are identical; the labels, the costs you record, and the suggested timeline differ by mode. The suggested timeline per mode is editable by SF or Admin in the settings (see Admin chapter).

Allocation and the departure lock

Allocation

SF allocates an order’s items to a shipment. Usually one PO travels on one shipment, but a shipment often carries several POs, and one PO can split across more than one shipment.

Departure lock

Items can be moved between shipments while the container has not left. Once it departs (Sailing for sea, In Flight for air), the contents lock: nothing can be added, removed or moved.

✓ Tip

A single PO can split across an air shipment and a sea shipment, for example urgent units fly while the bulk sails. Just create two shipments and allocate the right items to each.

chapters.title: Creating a Shipment
chapters.html:
SF creates a shipment when goods are ready to leave the factory. You capture the carrier and the real loading and sailing dates up front, and Manifest pre-fills the rest of the schedule.

Who
Solve Factory Admin
Where
Shipments → New shipment
Capture
Mode, carrier, loading & sailing dates, BL/AWB.
Then
Opens the shipment detail to manage it.

Creating a shipment

  1. New shipment. On the Shipments screen, click New shipment.
  2. Pick the mode. sea or air. The carrier list, date labels and the BL/AWB label all follow the mode.
  3. Choose the carrier. Pick the freight partner from the list (shown as code and company name). No carrier listed? Add it in Admin → Logistics partners.
  4. Enter the real dates. Loading date and Sailing date (for air, “Departure date”). These are the dates you actually know when booking.
  5. Add BL/AWB and container. The Bill of Lading or Air Waybill number, container type and number where known.
  6. Create shipment. Manifest opens the new shipment’s detail page.

How the dates pre-fill

From the sailing (or departure) date, Manifest suggests the downstream dates, arrival, customs clearance and delivery, using the timeline defaults for that mode. If you only enter a loading date, it works forward from there. These are suggestions, not locks: you can change any date afterwards on the detail page.

ⓘ Note

The timeline defaults (how many days each leg usually takes, per mode) are set by SF or Admin in Admin → Shipment timeline defaults. Tune them to match your real experience and every new shipment starts from sensible dates.

✓ Tip

You do not have to allocate items at creation. Create the shipment, then attach the orders it carries on the detail page (see Managing a Shipment).

chapters.title: Managing a Shipment
chapters.html:
The shipment detail page is where SF runs a container: advance its milestones, edit its details, attach the orders it carries, and (before it sails) move items around.

Who
Solve Factory Admin
Where
Shipments → click a shipment
Do
Advance, edit, allocate, move.
Locks
Contents freeze once it departs.

Advancing the journey

  1. Advance. The header shows the current stage and a stage strip. Click Advance to move to the next milestone (mode-aware: Sailing/Docked for sea, In Flight/Landed for air). Each advance date-stamps automatically.
  2. Received couples the order. When all of an order’s shipment legs reach Received, the order is recognised as delivered.

Editing details

  1. Edit. Opens the carrier, container, BL/AWB and all expected dates for change. Any date change is logged as a revision; the original plan is kept.
  2. Mode lock. You can change the mode only while the shipment is still Planned. Once it is loaded, the mode is fixed.

Allocating and moving items

  1. Add an order. In Allocated items, pick an order and click Add order; its lines join this container.
  2. Move between containers (before departure). While both shipments are pre-departure, items can be re-allocated. The order’s detail page also has a “Move this PO to another container” control.
⛔ Important

Once the shipment departs (Sailing or In Flight), its contents lock. Add and move are disabled and the page shows “contents locked”. This mirrors reality: a sailed container cannot be changed.

ⓘ Note

The Timeline card lists every event on the shipment, planned dates, revisions, stage advances and payments, with timestamps, so the full history is always visible.

chapters.title: Shipping Costs & Last-Mile Delivery
chapters.html:
When goods clear the port and again at last-mile delivery, SF records the logistics costs against the shipment. Each one deducts the shared pool the moment it is recorded. Last-mile also captures who is delivering and in which vehicle.

Who
Solve Factory Admin
Where
Shipment detail → Logistics costs & last-mile
Cost types
Shipping, customs, other fees, last-mile.
Pool
Drops immediately on each record.

Recording a logistics cost

  1. Record cost. On the shipment detail, in the costs card, click Record cost.
  2. Pick the type. shipping, customs, other_fees or last_mile.
  3. Enter the rupee amount. Then confirm. The pool drops by that amount immediately.

Air freight is priced by chargeable weight and sea by container or volume, but you record the final rupee figure either way; Manifest just prompts you for the right set of costs for the mode.

✓ Tip

If a cost pushes the pool negative, Manifest nudges you to raise a draw-down. It is a funding prompt, not a block.

Last-mile: who is bringing it

At the local-transport stage, capture who is doing the last-mile delivery and the vehicle number, so the store team knows exactly who and what vehicle to expect when the material arrives.

  1. Last-mile. Click Last-mile on the shipment.
  2. Pick the partner. Choose the delivery partner from the list (code and company name).
  3. Enter the vehicle number. Then Save. It shows on the shipment for the store team.
⛔ Important

Delivery partners are always chosen from the shared list, never typed as loose text. If the partner is not listed, add it once in Admin → Logistics partners, then pick it. This keeps the partner master clean.

parts.subtitle: Funding the pool, asking for funds, invoicing, and reading the running account.

chapters.title: LOT to SF Payments & Draw-downs
chapters.html:
LOT funds the shared pool by recording its wires to Solve Factory. When the pool runs low, SF (or LOT) raises a draw-down: a request for LOT to top it up.

Who
LOT records wires · SF raises draw-downs
Where
Payments · Draw-downs
Wire effect
Pool goes up (a credit).
UTR
Required on every new wire.

Recording a LOT to SF wire

  1. Open Payments. Click Record Wire.
  2. Enter the amount and UTR. The rupee amount and the bank UTR (reference) are both required.
  3. Set the channel and method. Which SF payout channel received it, and how it was sent.
  4. Record wire. The pool goes up by that amount; SF is now holding more of LOT’s money.
⛔ Important

Every new wire must carry a UTR. This is how the wire is matched to the bank later. Older historical payments may not have one, but all new ones do.

Raising a draw-down

A draw-down is a request for LOT to put money into the pool, usually because an upcoming payment (an advance, a balance, shipping) would otherwise push the pool negative.

  1. Raise Draw-down. From the Draw-downs screen, or from the prompt that appears after a payment runs the pool low.
  2. Pick the phase and order. Goods advance, shipping & customs, local, or other; optionally tag it to a specific order.
  3. Enter the amount. Manifest shows the Yuan equivalent at the current rate. Submit.
ⓘ Note

A draw-down is a funding prompt, not a payment and not a gate. It does not move the pool by itself; LOT settles it by recording a wire. SF can always pay from its own pocket and let the pool go negative.

chapters.title: Invoicing & Closing an Order
chapters.html:
Invoicing is how SF closes an order out, with a formal SF to LOT invoice for LOT’s books and GST. It is a record, not the thing that moves the money: goods and logistics already left the pool as they were paid.

Who
Solve Factory Admin
Where
Order detail → Invoice & close
Partial
Bill some lines now, the rest later.
Pool impact
Only the optional commission.

Raising an invoice

  1. Open Invoice & close. On a delivered (or partly invoiced) order, the Invoice card lists the goods lines.
  2. Tick the lines to bill. Partial invoicing is allowed: bill some now and the rest later. Already-billed lines show their invoice number and cannot be billed twice.
  3. Set GST per line. Each line carries its own GST percent (defaults to 18). A single PO can mix items on different GST codes, so set each correctly.
  4. Optionally add commission. Toggle the SF 2.5% commission on or off for the invoice.
  5. Submit. Manifest assigns the invoice number automatically (the VWINV series), stamps each billed line, and updates the order’s state.

How the invoice is valued

Priced lines

A line with a per-unit Yuan price is valued as price times quantity times the exchange rate.

Lump-cost lines

Some items (moulds, machines, mixed sets) have no per-unit price. Those bill the order’s recorded rupee cost instead, so the order is still closeable.

Invoice number

Auto-assigned from the VWINV series; never typed by hand. The financial year rolls over automatically each April.

What invoicing moves

⛔ Important

The only thing invoicing debits from the pool is the 2.5% commission (if you include it). Goods and logistics already left the pool when they were paid. The GST on the invoice is a document and compliance figure; it is not a separate pool movement.

ⓘ Note

The order becomes Partially invoiced while some goods lines are still unbilled, and Invoiced (closed) once they all carry an invoice number.

chapters.title: The Running Account & Exchange Rates
chapters.html:
The Running Account is the single source of truth for who owes whom. It is the shared pool, shown as a ledger with a live balance. Exchange Rates is the reference rate Manifest uses; the actual bank rate is always set per payment.

Who
LOT SF Admin
Where
Running Account · Exchange Rates
Net
Positive = SF holds LOT funds; negative = LOT owes SF.
FX
Reference only; bank rate is per payment.

Reading the running account

Net position

The headline balance. Positive means Solve Factory holds LOT’s money; negative means LOT owes SF.

Credits

LOT to SF wires paid in.

Debits

Goods, logistics charges and commission that SF has spent.

Ledger

Every entry in order, with a running balance. Click a row to see its detail and jump to the linked record.

Opening balance and any carried-forward adjustments from prior years sit in the ledger as their own entries, so the net always reconciles.

Exchange rates

Reference rate

Manifest pulls a daily CNY to INR rate automatically. It is shown in the top bar and on the Exchange Rates screen for reference.

Manual override

An LOT user with FX rights can set a manual rate for a date when needed.

Actual bank rate

The rate that matters for money is the one you enter on each vendor payment. The reference rate never overrides it.

⛔ Important

When you record a vendor payment, always enter the actual bank rate you paid at. The reference rate is only a guide.

parts.subtitle: Finding orders, the evidence vault, and the settings that keep the system tuned.

chapters.title: Orders List, Search & Documents
chapters.html:
The Orders screen is where you find any order and open its detail. Documents is the shared evidence vault for PIs, invoices, bills of lading and receipts.

Who
LOT SF Admin
Where
Orders · Documents
Search
By order number or title.
Vault
Evidence, downloadable by signed link.

Finding an order

  1. Search. Type an order number or title in the search box; the list filters as you type and the dropdown jumps straight to a match.
  2. Read the columns. Order number, title, category, value, the Snorkel PO (if linked), state, balance due and date.
  3. Open it. Click any row to open its detail, where all the actions live.
State

Where the order is in its billing axis (in flight, delivered, partially invoiced, invoiced).

Balance

What is still due against the order, or paid when settled.

Documents

Every PI, invoice, bill of lading, packing list and wire receipt can be stored against its order or shipment. Filter by type, and download any file by a short-lived secure link.

Where files attach

From an order or shipment detail; the file is tagged to that record and a milestone is stamped for key types (like the PI).

Access

The vault is private. Downloads use a signed link that expires, so files are never publicly exposed.

✓ Tip

Attach the vendor PI and the bill of lading as you get them. They become part of the order’s timeline and make closing the order out clean and auditable.

chapters.title: Admin - Users, Timeline Defaults & Partners
chapters.html:
Admin is where LOT manages who can use Manifest, tunes the shipment timeline defaults, and keeps the logistics-partner master. Three small settings that keep the whole system accurate.

Who
Admin
Where
Admin
Manages
Users, timeline defaults, partners.
Audit
No audit on defaults; direct edits.

Users & roles

The Admin screen lists members grouped by organisation (Legend of Toys and Solve Factory) with their role and status.

  1. Onboard a Solve Factory owner. The SF owner first requests a login link on the sign-in screen (this creates their account). Then an admin adds them here and assigns the SF role.
  2. Assign or change a role. LOT finance / founder, SF owner, or admin. Roles control exactly what each person sees and can do.

Shipment timeline defaults

These are the day-offsets Manifest uses to pre-fill a new shipment’s expected dates, set separately for sea and air.

  1. Edit the offsets. For each mode, set how many days after the previous milestone each leg usually takes (loaded, sailing, docked, cleared, local transport, received).
  2. Save. New shipments now pre-fill from these. They are suggestions only; SF can change any date on a shipment.
ⓘ Note

These defaults are edited directly with no audit trail, on purpose; they are tuning knobs, not records. Adjust them whenever your real lead times change.

Logistics partners

The shared list of carriers and last-mile transporters (freight forwarders, shipping lines, couriers). Every carrier and last-mile picker in Manifest reads from this master.

  1. Add a partner. Click Add partner, enter the company, country and the modes it supports (sea, air, land), plus IATA or SCAC codes and a tracking URL where relevant.
  2. Create. Manifest assigns the partner code. It is now selectable everywhere.
⛔ Important

Partners are never typed as free text anywhere in Manifest. If a needed carrier or transporter is missing, add it here once. This keeps the master clean and the pickers reliable.

ⓘ Note

Vendors come from the shared LOT vendor master and already cover China, international and domestic suppliers, so there is nothing to set up here for vendors.
